problems: The blind guess's primary reading (a human dancer or leaper) is wrong. Only the alternative 'bird or winged creature in flight' fits the intended Pole-Runner, so the figure does not read as its subject at first glance.

The neck is too long. The gap between crown of the head (94302, about 350,132) and breast (94779, about 338,230) is much longer than the body, so the head looks detached and the figure looks like a stick figure rather than a bird.

The body is a thin diagonal line from breast down to lower body (96441, about 261,320). There is no torso mass, and the belly star (95853, about 290,278) sits on the wing root, so the widest point is not visible as a body shape.

Wings are asymmetric and disconnected from the body. The left wing runs from left wrist (98571, about 153,320) out to the left wingtip (99675, about 89,407), but the right wing is a wide triangle from belly to right wingtip (92689, about 447,289) and down to right outer primary (93408, about 425,397). The two wings do not read as a matched pair spread in flight.

The tail fork is cramped. The left fork tip (97165) and the tail notch (96825) sit almost on top of each other near (222,458) and (240,448), and their labels overlap the gold lines and each other, so the fork is hard to read.
Gold lines are correct as a skeleton, and the blue outline is a real silhouette, not a copy of the gold lines. The figure is upright, with beak at top and tail at bottom.
